column1: # Official media to fetch from the Internet Archive and, when asked, extract
# name <TAB> archive.org item <TAB> file pattern <TAB> corpus output dir <TAB> action [<TAB> exclude regex]
# A push that changes this file starts .github/workflows/import-media.yml,
# which fetches every entry that is not fetched yet, inventories it, and
# imports the documentation pages of the entries whose action is `import`
# or `import-scratch`; already fetched media is never downloaded twice and an
# already extracted component is skipped.
#   inventory        download (if needed) + list what the medium holds
#   import           ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is kept verbatim under sources/<name>/ with a
#                    PROVENANCE.md
#   import-scratch   ... and copy its documentation into the corpus; the
#                    medium is fetched to .cache/media/ and thrown away again
#                    (an InstallShield-era installer disc is ~40 MB of mostly
#                    binaries and samples - the corpus keeps pages, not media)
#   inventory-scratch
#                    download and list what the medium holds, then throw the
#                    medium away: for a disc that is only being considered
# A finished import is recorded in data/reports/media-imported.tsv, so a later
# run does not download an image it has already imported (the scratch medium is
# gone by then); `--force` overrides it.
# Either way only documentation is imported: this is a documentation corpus,
# so a medium's source files, headers, samples and toolchains are counted in
# the inventory and skipped (see "What is collected" in the top-level README).
# The 6th field refuses documentation files that are not documentation of the
# product: the exclude below drops infoview.hlp, the SDK disc's 1,236-page help
# for the InfoViewer/Visual C++ viewer UI itself (dialog boxes, wizard fields,
# editor options).  It is Microsoft help, but it is not Windows CE material.
# windbg.hlp (the CE debugger reference) and the disc's readme stay.
# windows-ce-2.0-sdk: Microsoft Windows CE Platform SDK (H/PC) 2.0 (02/98) -
# the CE 2.0 SDK whose Books Online the corpus has been looking for since the
# CE 2.0 Technical Information CD turned out to carry no API reference (see
# sources/windows-ce-2.0/PROVENANCE.md).  The disc is an InstallShield
# installer: the documentation is inside data1.cab/_sys1.cab, which the
# workflow unpacks with `unshield` (7z cannot read InstallShield cabinets).
# The first import attempt downloaded and inventoried the disc but imported
# nothing (7z cannot read those cabinets, and the inventory then crashed on the
# extensionless files of the disc - fixed in tools/import-media.py).
windows-ce-2.0-sdk
# The DevCon '99 conference CD (1999): the Windows CE Developers Conference
# disc.  338 MB / 1,689 files; the disc carries the Windows CE 2.11/2.12 SDK,
# DDK and Platform Builder documentation (wcesdkr/, wceddk/, wcesdkg/,
# wceapc/, ...) next to the conference's own material, and only the
# documentation of the product is imported:
#   * the whole conference folder (Windows_CE_Developers_Conference_..._CD/)
#     is refused - it is the sponsors' shop window (Kingston, Casio, Compaq,
#     ... press releases and product sheets), the Win32/ATL sample trees and
#     their readme pages, not Microsoft documentation of Windows CE;
#   * MPLAYER2/ is the Books Online of the desktop Windows Media Player 2,
#     MPSUPP/ is the generic Microsoft Product Support Services guide,
#     ACCESSIB/ is Microsoft's general accessibility material and Handhelds/
#     is a vendor's Palm-size PC specification sheets - none of them document
#     Windows CE;
#   * FrontPage metadata directories (_vti_cnf/ and friends) are refused by
#     tools/import-media.py itself.
# With those out, the import brings in the CE 2.11/2.12 SDK documentation
# (6,382 pages; see corpus/msdn-library/wcedevcon-99/PROVENANCE.md).
# The first import run died at its first CHM (tools/extract-chm.py is loaded by
# path now, and the workflow caches .cache/media so a retry does not fetch the
# 338 MB image again).
wcedevcon-99
# --- 2026-10-20 harvest expansion: inventory first ---------------------------
# The four media below are the candidates sources/README.md has carried
# since 2026-10; the archive.org identifiers and file forms were
# verified against the item pages on 2026-10-20 (see
# docs/cegcc-survey.ja.md's harvest notes and queues/third-party-sources.md).
# All four enter as inventory-scratch: download, list what the medium
# holds (the listing lands in data/reports/media-last.txt), discard.
# Whether any documentation is imported -- and with which exclude
# regex -- is decided only after reading that inventory.
# CAUTION (standing rule): the Platform Builder discs also carry
# shared-source trees and SDK headers.  Those are never corpus
# material (docs/COLLECTION-POLICY.md: documentation only; the
# importer counts and skips source/binaries, and check-policy.py
# keeps the source-or-binary count at 0).  Only documentation pages
# (HTML/CHM doc sets) may ever flip one of these rows to import.
# windows-ce-5.0-cd5: Windows Embedded CE 5.0 CD5 (English), item
# en_win_ce_net_cd5, single 478.8 MB ISO (verified 2026-10-20).  The
# CE 5.0 set's later disc; expected to hold platform documentation
# beyond what CD1's CHMs (corpus/chm/windows-ce-5.0/) already gave.
windows-ce-5.0-cd5
# windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r2: the CE 6.0 R2 update (Microsoft Download
# id 18111), item windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r2, CE6R2.iso 1.9 GB
# (verified 2026-10-20).  R2 refreshed the Platform Builder 6.0
# documentation set.
windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r2
# windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r3: the CE 6.0 R3 update (Microsoft Download
# id 14226), item CE6R3, CE6R3.iso 1.1 GB (verified 2026-10-20).  R3
# documentation includes the .NET Compact Framework 3.5 reference.
windows-embedded-ce-6.0-r3
# windows-embedded-ce-6.0-pb-sp1: Platform Builder 6.0 SP1 ("Tools
# SP1", Microsoft Download id 4097), item
# windows-embedded-ce-6.0-platform-builder-sp1, 56.6 MB installer
# package (verified 2026-10-20; the exact installer filename is what
# the inventory will show -- the pattern below accepts the usual
# forms).
windows-embedded-ce-6.0-pb-sp1
